solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bird seen on mounds regularly is a foreshore frequenter

indicators.note: in an across clue the bird sits after, i.e. on, the letters from the mounds
taking every other letter of the word mounds, starting with the first

parts.note: the lark is a common songbird

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher spots something perched on the mounds and wonders if it is a beach-loving species.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' looks like the definition but it is only part of the wordplay; the definition is the tidal-shore scavenger at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A mudlark was someone who scavenged the Thames mud at low tide, so a regular on the foreshore.

clue.text: Millions favoured tsar as a mover of people

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million(s)
in favour, popular, is IN
Ivan the Terrible was a Russian tsar

explanation.surface: A rich, favoured tsar is hailed as someone who moved his people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mover of people' suggests a leader stirring the masses; it is a vehicle carrying passengers.
explanation.definitionFit: A small passenger van carries a group of people, so it literally transports them.

clue.text: Assist rising clan in forceful attack

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word for assist is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to assist is to aid
a clan is a tribe

explanation.surface: Helping a clan that is rising up in a violent assault.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter verbal onslaught, a fierce attack in words.

clue.text: Supermarket division is cutting beer

indicators.note: the little word is cuts into the beer, sitting inside it

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A shop layout note: one section of the store slices into the beer display.
explanation.definitionFit: Shelves in a supermarket are separated into walkways, each one a distinct section.

clue.text: Author (not English) has new name for English town

indicators.note: not English means the abbreviation for English is removed from the author

parts.note: Kingsley Amis was an English novelist

explanation.surface: A non-English author gives an English town a fresh name.
explanation.walkthrough: KING'S LYNN is a market town in Norfolk, in the east of England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norfolk port is a town in England, an example of the category given.

clue.text: Expertise with frying pan, though dropping the last two

indicators.note: the final pair of letters is removed from the word for a frying pan

parts.note: a skillet is a frying pan

explanation.surface: A cook's expertise with the frying pan, albeit losing a couple at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Skill and expertise are synonyms: practised ability at something.

clue.text: Listen out for mum

indicators.note: out signals the letters of listen are put out of order

explanation.surface: A child is told to keep an ear out for their mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like mother, but here it means quiet, as in keeping mum.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep mum is to stay quiet, so mum is an adjective for saying nothing.

clue.text: To butt in, changing spades to no trumps, is impolite

indicators.note: changing one thing to another means replacing it, here a letter in the word is

parts.note: S is the bridge abbreviation for spades
NT is the bridge abbreviation for no trumps
impolite means rude

explanation.surface: A bridge-table etiquette rule: interrupting by switching your bid from spades to no trumps is bad manners.
explanation.walkthrough: The bridge scene suggests the bid itself; in fact the S in IS becomes NT.
explanation.definitionFit: To intrude is to butt in, both meaning to barge into something uninvited.

clue.text: Noted traveller in train to Petrograd, returning 9.50?

definitions.text: Noted traveller in train to Petrograd

indicators.note: returning means the letters from the number are read backwards

parts.note: 9 is NINE and 50 is L in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A historic passenger on a train to Petrograd, coming back on the 9.50 service.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1917 Lenin crossed Germany to Russia in a sealed train. 9.50 looks like a train time but is NINE plus L.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bolshevik leader famously travelled by sealed train back to revolutionary Petrograd in April 1917.

clue.text: Near a very quiet fish

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very quiet
the roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: An angler creeps close to a fish in total silence.
explanation.definitionFit: To approach and to near are synonymous verbs meaning to come closer.

clue.text: Himalayan creature literally covering two fifths of Nepal?

definitions.text: Himalayan creature literally covering two fifths of Nepal?

parts.words: Himalayan creature literally covering two fifths of Nepal?
parts.note: spell out that pair literally, with the joining word, and a mountain animal appears

explanation.surface: A mountain animal whose range spans a sizeable chunk of Nepal.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken literally, the answer covers two of NEPAL's five letters: P and A. The red panda really does live in Nepal.
explanation.definitionFit: The red panda lives in the Himalayan forests of Nepal, India and China.

clue.text: Just one garment being worn

parts.note: a singlet is a sleeveless vest
clothes being worn are on

explanation.surface: Someone wearing only a single item of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: A singlet is a vest, an undershirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A singleton is a single individual thing, just one rather than a pair or group.

clue.text: Dream I must be held in respect

indicators.note: the letter I goes inside the word for respect

parts.note: to revere is to respect deeply

explanation.surface: A dreamy vow: I ought to be held in high esteem.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverie is a daydream, a state of pleasant absorbed musing.

clue.text: Browning university substituted for two pieces of interminable Swinburne

indicators.note: a letter takes the place of two letters from the trimmed poet's name
without its end, so the poet's name loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A literary swap: Browning in place of a slice of Swinburne, two Victorian poets.
explanation.walkthrough: Browning looks like the poet Robert Browning; it is skin turning brown. Swinburne loses its last E, then U replaces WI.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunburn is skin reddened or tanned by the sun, a kind of browning.

clue.text: Queen of Lebanon in the wars backing the old knight

indicators.note: a person in the wars is battered, so the letters of Lebanon are knocked about
backing means the old word for the is turned round

parts.note: ye is an archaic form of the
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A queen from war-torn Lebanon supports an old knight.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry VIII's second wife was Queen of England before her execution in 1536.

clue.text: Frequently after deepest North Sea port

indicators.note: the word for frequently comes after the word for deepest

parts.note: deepest can mean lowest
oft is a poetic word for often

explanation.surface: A sailor's lore: often found right after the deepest waters off a North Sea harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: LOWESTOFT is a port in Suffolk, England's most easterly town.
explanation.definitionFit: The Suffolk town stands on the North Sea coast and is a fishing harbour.

clue.text: Nice wine encapsulates European mood

indicators.note: the French wine wraps around the abbreviation, holding it inside

parts.note: in Nice, a French city, wine is vin

explanation.surface: A pleasant glass of wine puts a European in a good humour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Vein can mean a mood or tone, as in speaking in a light-hearted vein.

clue.text: Denial — for example in what might be Scotland?

indicators.note: the abbreviation for example sits in the country word

parts.note: Scotland is an example of a nation

explanation.surface: A political denial about whether Scotland ought to be independent.
explanation.definitionFit: Negation is the act of denying or contradicting, so denial is a synonym.

clue.text: Just like rugby players, say, to belt out full of alcohol

indicators.note: the singing word is full of the drink, holding it inside

parts.note: to belt out a song is to sing
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Rugby players famously belting out songs after a skinful.
explanation.walkthrough: Sporting means both fair-minded (just) and to do with sport, like rugby players.
explanation.definitionFit: Sporting means fair and generous, and also describes people who play sports, as rugby players do.

clue.text: Expect he's keeping in work

indicators.note: the pronoun keeps the work word inside it

parts.note: he is, so the word he is the one doing the keeping
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: An employer expects him to stay at his job.
explanation.definitionFit: To hope is to look forward to something, close in sense to expecting it.

clue.text: Present suits are becoming dated

parts.note: the four suits make up a pack of cards
to age is to grow old, becoming dated

explanation.surface: Today's suits are already going out of fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like an adjective (current); it is a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A parcel is a wrapped gift, so a present is the item sent or given.

clue.text: Bird ringing expedition finished amid flapping wingspan

indicators.note: the word for finished goes in the middle of the jumbled wingspan
flapping wings move about, so the letters of wingspan are jumbled

parts.note: time is up when it is finished

explanation.surface: A ringing trip ends among birds beating their wings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flapping' scrambles the fodder to give SWANPING. Swan upping is the annual July census of Thames swans, when cygnets are caught and marked.
explanation.definitionFit: The annual Thames ceremony catches and marks swans, rather like a ringing survey of birds.

clue.text: Tax cine reels? Not right

indicators.note: reels means staggers, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A tax on cinema film reels gets the verdict that it is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reels' looks like film reels to go with cine; here it means staggers.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inexact is imprecise, so not quite correct.

clue.text: Smoked reefer to take dope with daughter

parts.note: to do someone is to swindle or take them
gen is information, as is dope

explanation.surface: A drug user lights a joint with their daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' suggests drugs but here means information (GEN); a dog-end is a cigarette butt.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog-end is the stub left of a smoked cigarette, which a smoked reefer becomes.

clue.text: Giant penny-farthing with no rear wheel? "Penny Singular"

indicators.note: without its back end, so the bike word loses its final letter

parts.note: a penny-farthing is an early bicycle, a cycle
O is the shape of a wheel
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A huge old penny-farthing bicycle missing its back wheel, dubbed the Penny Singular.
explanation.walkthrough: The giant has one eye, as the bike with no rear wheel has one; Cyclops was a one-eyed giant of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Cyclops was a one-eyed giant, such as Polyphemus.

clue.text: Copper retiring is comfortably off

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a retiring person is shy

explanation.surface: A police officer heading into retirement is well provided for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a police officer; it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cushy means easy and comfortable, as in a cushy job that leaves one well provided for.

clue.text: Farmland animals eating five tons in gathered crops

indicators.note: the animals take the Roman five inside them

parts.note: hares live on open farmland
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Hares in the fields munch their way through tons of the crop.
explanation.definitionFit: A harvest is the crop gathered in at the end of the growing season.

clue.text: Buzz coming with a northern person

parts.note: a buzz is a hum

explanation.surface: A buzzing sound arrives together with a northerner.
explanation.definitionFit: A human is a person, a member of humankind.

clue.text: Old money gets the reverse of low cabin — the best on board

parts.note: the stater was an ancient Greek coin

indicators.note: the cow's sound is written backwards

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

explanation.surface: An old-money passenger books the opposite of a cheap cabin: the finest on the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' looks like the opposite of best; it is the cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: A stateroom is a private cabin on a ship, usually the most luxurious.

clue.text: State of Florida holidays?

indicators.note: of signals the letters are part of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A question about one of Florida's holiday resorts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' wants to point at Florida; the answer is another US state, sitting across the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the fifty United States, in the northwest.

clue.text: Product that's widely drunk without whisky

indicators.note: drunk means the remaining letters are staggered about
without means the letter for whisky is removed

parts.note: Whisky is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A popular drink that is drunk everywhere without any whisky in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whisky' looks like the drink but is the phonetic-alphabet letter W.
explanation.definitionFit: A yield is the output or amount produced, such as a crop or return.

clue.text: Child's brought in near the end of today

indicators.note: the word for near is brought inside the child word

parts.note: a tot is a small child
nigh is an old word for near

explanation.surface: A child is brought indoors as evening draws on.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonight is the evening of the present day, its closing part.
